To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RecA-DNA filaments are capable of accommodating an additional single strand or double strand of DNA, and that the DNA-binding, annealig and recombinational properties of the complexes are determined by the nature of the incoming DNA molecule.
RecA protein forms stable complexes with DNA in the absence of nucleotides.
RecA helical filament complexes can bind two DNA molecules and that the two DNA binding regions in RecA helical polymers are equivalent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the DNA binding properties of stable RecA-saturated complexes formed with single-, double- or triple-stranded DNA.
the molecular mechanism of RecA-mediated homology-dependent DNA strand exchange.
the mechanism by which RecA protein interacts with DNA and with the consequences of this interaction for the initiation of homologous re combination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

RecA is a protein with two DNA binding sites, each of them able to interact with a single-stranded DNA or a double-stranded DNA, and that these DNA binding sites are located within a single helical filament of the protein.
RecA helical filament has two DNA binding sites which are occupied by either single-stranded or double-stranded DNAs, depending on the nature of the DNA used for the formation of the complexes.
the two DNA binding regions in the RecA filament are occupied by DNA molecules of the same polarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a RecA helical filament, once formed, can bind to DNA with two different DNA binding sites and that this binding is independent of homology between the DNA molecules.

RecA-DNA interactions are not restricted to a simple one-to-one binding between RecA and DNA but that the DNA-binding properties of the protein are much more complex and involve the cooperative binding of two DNA molecules within RecA filaments.

RecA-DNA interactions can be divided into three steps, i.e. polymerization of RecA on single-stranded DNA, formation of a stable complex with double-stranded DNA, and initiation of homologous recombiantion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RecA helical filament can accommodate two DNA molecules in a way that is compatible with their recombination.
RecA-DNA interactions are highly flexible and can accommodate a large number of DNA structures.
